info.title: acme/alerts/v1/alerts.proto
info.description:
Contract between the VS Code extension and the Go backend.

The backend serves gRPC; grpc-gateway projects the same service onto the
JSON/HTTP paths in the google.api.http annotations below, and that projection
is what the extension talks to. See docs/DESIGN.md §5 for the gateway
specifics the client depends on (streaming envelope, JSON field naming,
status-code mapping).

post.summary: Records the user's answer. Idempotent on idempotency_key.

get.summary:
Fallback for environments where the streaming response is buffered by a
proxy, and the catch-up call made on activation before subscribing.
Blocks up to wait_seconds for an alert to arrive; returns immediately if
any are already pending.

parameters.name: waitSeconds
parameters.description: 0 returns immediately. Capped server-side; 30 is the client's default.

get.summary:
Validates the token, confirms the client_id is known, and reports the
minimum client version the server will accept. Called once on activation.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description:
Opaque routing identifier read from the client-id file on the user's
machine (docs/DESIGN.md §6). Not a credential: the bearer token is. The
server MUST verify that the presented token is authorized for this
client_id, or any token holder could receive another client's alerts.

get.summary: Long-lived server stream of alerts and lifecycle events.
get.description:
Over grpc-gateway this is a chunked HTTP response carrying one JSON object
per line, each wrapped as {"result": <Event>}. It is NOT Server-Sent
Events: there is no "data:" framing and no EventSource-compatible
reconnect. Resumption is by last_sequence, not the Last-Event-ID header.

parameters.name: lastSequence
parameters.description:
Highest Event.sequence the client has already processed. The server
replays everything after it. Zero (or absent) means "send me everything
currently outstanding".

parameters.name: clientVersion
parameters.description:
Reported so the server can log version skew against a fleet it cannot
update. Advisory only.

post.summary:
Aborts a change that is still within its cancellation window
(MachineChange.cancellable_until). Past that point the server returns
FAILED_PRECONDITION and the change runs to completion.

get.summary:
Everything the form needs to render: the GPU catalogue, the machine's
current configuration, the numeric bounds, and any change already in
flight. One call, so the form cannot render half-configured.

post.summary:
Applies a new configuration to the machine directly — there is no approval
step. Idempotent on idempotency_key, and guarded by expected_version so a
form rendered from stale data cannot silently clobber a concurrent change.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the change is accepted; completion arrives as a
MachineConfigChanged event on the stream.

post.summary:
Computes what applying a spec would do, without doing it: whether it needs
a restart, which specific edits force that, and any validation errors.
post.description:
Called immediately before the confirmation dialog, so the dialog states
real consequences rather than guesses. Restarts are NOT required by every
change, and only the server knows which ones need one. This doubles as
pre-flight validation: the user should never confirm a change that is then
rejected.

buttonId.description: Set only when outcome is ANSWERED; must match one of the alert's buttons.

idempotencyKey.description:
Generated once per user action and reused across retries. Replaying the
same key returns the original result; a different answer to an already
answered alert is ABORTED (409).

modal.description:
Blocks the editor until answered. Expensive to the user's attention;
reserve for alerts that genuinely cannot wait.

buttons.description:
Zero to two. The client truncates anything longer rather than failing,
and synthesises an "OK" button if empty — a VS Code notification without
buttons auto-hides and would be missed.

v1AlertOutcome.description:
- ALERT_OUTCOME_DISMISSED: The user closed the notification without choosing a button. Reported so
the server can distinguish "seen and ignored" from "never delivered"; the
alert stays outstanding.

reason.description: Shown to the user if the alert was on screen. Optional.

v1AlertRevoked.description:
Alerts have no client-side expiry: an unanswered alert persists across
restarts until the user answers it or the server withdraws it with this.

spec.description:
The complete desired configuration, not a delta. The server diffs it
against what is current; sending the whole spec means an old client and a
new server cannot disagree about which fields were "left alone".

idempotencyKey.description:
Generated once per apply attempt and reused across retries, so a response
lost to a dropped connection can be replayed safely.

expectedVersion.description:
GetMachineConfigResponse.version the form was rendered from. A mismatch is
ABORTED (409) and the client refetches and shows what changed, rather than
overwriting it.

serverTime.description:
Anchor for rendering the cancellation countdown without depending on how
recently a heartbeat arrived.

fieldPath.description:
Proto path of the changed field, e.g. "spec.ram_gb". Matches the paths
used in google.rpc.BadRequest violations, so the client has one mapping
from path to input.

description.description:
Human-readable, shown beside the field's before/after in the dialog,
e.g. "Requires a restart".

v1ChangeStatus.description:
- CHANGE_STATUS_FAILED: Machine is back on its previous configuration.
 - CHANGE_STATUS_CANCELLING: Cancel accepted, revert in progress.
 - CHANGE_STATUS_CANCELLED: Cancelled and reverted. Terminal, and indistinguishable from FAILED in
its effect on the machine — the distinction is whose decision it was.

sequence.description:
Monotonically increasing per client_id, gapless. The client persists the
highest value it has handled and sends it back as last_sequence on
reconnect.

heartbeat.description:
Sent every 25s so the client can distinguish a quiet server from a
half-open connection. Carries no meaning beyond its arrival.

machineConfigChanged.description:
A configuration change finished applying, failed, or was made by
somebody else. The form refreshes its current values from this rather
than polling.

minClientVersion.description:
Semver. The extension is distributed as a .vsix passed around by hand, so
it never auto-updates; this is how an out-of-date install is told to
update rather than failing in confusing ways.

version.description:
Opaque version of the machine's configuration state. Echoed back as
ApplyMachineConfigRequest.expected_version; the server rejects a mismatch.
This is what stops a form left open for an hour from reverting a change
somebody made in the meantime.

gpuTypes.description:
Rendered in the order given; the client does not re-sort. Must include the
reserved "none" id. The client synthesises it when absent, and logs a
warning: a form with no way to say "no GPU" is broken.

current.description:
The machine's current configuration. This is what the form is pre-filled
with and what "changed" is measured against. Absent only for a machine
that has never been configured.

limits.description:
Absent means the documented defaults apply: 1-256 cores, 1-2048 GB RAM,
1-2048 GB SSD, 1-8 GPUs. Sending them explicitly means a bound can change
without shipping a new .vsix.

pendingChange.description:
Set while a change is applying. The client renders the form read-only
rather than letting the user queue a second change on top of the first.

gpuTypeId.description: "none" is reserved and means no GPU.

maxCount.description:
Upper bound on gpu_count for this type. Node topologies differ per
accelerator, so this is per-type rather than a single global maximum. The
client clamps to min(max_count, limits.gpu_count_max).

sequence.description:
Highest sequence represented by this response, so a client that fell back
to polling can resume streaming without a gap.

cancellableUntil.description:
Deadline for CancelMachineChange. Absent when the change was never
cancellable or the window has closed. The client renders a countdown from
this, corrected for clock skew against the server time it tracks from
heartbeats — and treats its own countdown as advisory, since the server
is the authority on whether a cancel arrived in time.

failureReason.description:
Set when status is FAILED. Shown to the user verbatim, so it should read
as an explanation rather than a stack trace.

A failed or cancelled change leaves the machine on its previous
configuration — the server reverts, and there is no partial state for the
client to represent or the user to untangle.

url.description:
Deep link to the change record, offered as an "Open" button on the
completion notification. Optional.

version.description: New config version, to be used as expected_version on the next apply.

change.description:
The change that produced this state. Absent when the change originated
outside this client, which is exactly when the client most needs to know
its form is stale.

spec.description:
The complete desired configuration, exactly as it would be sent to
ApplyMachineConfig.

hasChanges.description:
False when the spec is identical to the current configuration. The client
disables Apply in that state anyway, so this is a backstop.

requiresRestart.description:
True when applying this particular spec restarts the machine. Not a
property of the machine: growing a disk may be free where swapping an
accelerator is not.

effects.description:
One per field the user changed, so the confirmation dialog can name which
specific edit forces the restart rather than warning about the change as
an undifferentiated whole.

warning.title:
Optional extra sentence for the dialog, e.g. "Running jobs will be
terminated."

cancellationWindowSeconds.description:
How long the change will be cancellable once started, so the dialog can
set expectations before the user commits. Zero means not cancellable.

gpuCount.description:
Absent when gpu_type_id is "none" — not zero. A request that sets both is
rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than silently ignoring the field, so
a bug in the client's conditional logic surfaces immediately instead of
quietly provisioning the wrong thing.

recorded.description:
True when this call recorded the answer, false when it matched an answer
already on file. Lets the client tell a successful retry from a genuine
double-submit without treating either as an error.
